comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
Using `\s+` as hidden rule would make `NEWLINE` rule useless, see https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/4751#discussion_r1326219022.

So it won't tokenize `TitleAndAccessibilities` or `NEWLINE+`.

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
Please add the `Diagram` prefix (which is here `Packet`) for specific diagram rules; using them without that prefix may interfere with other diagram rules or even AST (there is a diagram called `Block` :) )

And the Semicolon in a newline is a convention I'm just using following :)

```suggestion
  blocks+=PacketBlock*
;

PacketBlock:
```

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
The `NEWLINE+` is to prohibited users from adding multiple blocks in the same line, e.g.:

```
packet-beta
1: "string" 2: "string"
```

And the Semicolon in a newline is a convention I'm just using following :)

```suggestion
    start=INT ('-' end=INT)? ':' label=STRING NEWLINE+
;
```

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
> @aloisklink are types inferred from defaults or should we explicitly state them anyway?

Officially, if there is no `type` field, any type should be allowed (if the `json-schema-to-typescript` converter is using `typeof` the `default` value instead of `any`, I believe this is technically wrong).

For documentation/TypeScript purposes, I would definitely recommend putting in an explicit type, so people know not to put in strings/arrays/objects into these types.

Btw, if you want to limit a value to just positive integers, you can write:

```yaml
type: integer
minimum: 0
```
